title: ISO/IEC Directives, Part 2: Principles and rules for the structure and drafting of ISO and IEC documents
source: ISO/IEC Directives, Part 2, ninth edition (Edition 9.0, 2021-05), clause 7 "Verbal forms for expressions of provisions" (7.2 to 7.6), read 2026-10-08.

rules.text: A requirement is written with shall, and a prohibition with shall not.
Must does not stand in for shall; it marks a constraint that comes from outside the document.
A recommendation is written with should.
A permission is written with may, not with can or might.
A possibility or a capability is written with can, not with may.
May not is never used for a prohibition; a negative permission is rewritten as what is allowed or as a requirement.
